text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as crude oil prices spiked sharply on geopolitical tension. Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, sending U.S. crude up to around $102 per barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices mean higher revenues and profitability on the barrels they pump and sell.

The move also reflects a broader supply tightness: the gap between U.S. and global oil prices has widened significantly (U.S. crude at $102 versus Brent at $126.55), and physical delivery costs have surged due to tanker rate spikes, effectively making crude more valuable. This two-week rally of 15.6% for the stock tracks the climb in oil prices as Middle East tensions have mounted, reinforcing the direct link between geopolitical risk premiums and energy producer valuations.
